name: Xīn Jiàn Xiá Qíngyuán
storyline:
The Legend of Swordman is a reimagining of Seasun’s 1997 role-playing game Sword Heroes' Fate. Set during the war-torn Southern Song Dynasty, it unfolds a series of martial arts conflicts and entanglements in the world of Jianghu (the martial arts community). The cast features both historical figures—such as Yue Fei, Han Shizhong, Liang Hongyu, and Qin Hui as well as legendary martial heroes like Dugu Jian, Zhang Linxin, Zhang Rumeng, Nangong Caihong, and Yang Ying. In addition to continuing the rich and visually splendid features of the series, this installment also introduces the concept of hidden weapons.

Unlike Sword Heroes' Fate 2, which focused more on a personal narrative, The Legend of Swordman is grounded in the turbulent historical backdrop of the Southern Song Dynasty. It uses this real historical setting to unveil one dramatic martial arts tale after another.

The story takes place during the Southern Song era. In the autumn of 1126, the Jin Dynasty launched a major invasion of the Northern Song. Not long after, Emperor Huizong and Emperor Qinzong were captured—an event historically known as the "Jingkang Incident". The following March, Huizong’s ninth son, Prince Zhao Gou, proclaimed himself emperor in Nanjing, later relocating to Lin’an. With only half the country under control, the Southern Song struggled to survive. Fortunately, patriotic generals like Yue Fei and Han Shizhong led their troops in fierce resistance, saving what remained of the dynasty.

Little known to most is that during this time, many martial artists of the Jianghu also sacrificed their lives for the Song Dynasty, writing a heroic and tragic chapter in history. In the year 1139, word arrives of the assassination of the Jin Prime Minister Da Lan…
